sentences.sentence: The BATFE was a state funded agency, and all their papers were government funded.
That information alone was worth more to them than all the oil and uranium in Alaska and that was a pretty safe bet.
I had a feeling we'd be needing that information in the near future.
I could see people coming out of their houses with rifles and some with handguns.
I didn't waste time counting how many I could see.
I just headed for the door and into the hall.
Just a second after I walked out, I saw the first one explode, and my heart almost stopped.
I don't think anybody but me even noticed.
There were four on each side of the house; and I didn't have a gun with me so I figured I was the first out the door, which meant one less lander for them to come back for.
I had to make a choice; head for the front or the back door.
There were people in the back already; but the doors were made of concrete block, the front door was wood, and I had the best chance of getting away with it by going out the back.
So I ran back to the front door and into the back yard.
I found it had collapsed, with a couple of people there.
I heard more impacts.
This was one of their landers, that couldn't take the stress of the lander coming down.
I think I was just a little surprised, and I started to check it out, when more impacts went off; I guess I didn't have enough sense of humor about this.
I looked up, and it was the one that had fallen in the front yard; and it was on its side.
I went over there and looked inside.
It was already opening, and the men inside had already gotten out and disappeared.

sentences.sentence: it was obvious she did not approve of his recent creation of man.
But then she was always quick to criticize.
The Norse god Loki was there, his mouth twisted into a sneer.
He had always looked displeased with God, so God was hardly surprised to see him among the onlookers.
The Greek gods were there, too.
The Chinese, Indian, and Japanese gods, all of them, were there.
The Roman and Celtic gods, the Norse gods, and the Egyptian, too.
They all stared with eyes wide and ears burning.
It was the most God had ever seen them at odds with one another, which was to say a whole lot.
God yelled into the crowd.
Everyone turned and looked at him, and God sighed.
He had hoped he could go upstairs and ignore this until they'd run out of energy and gone back to their own quarrels, but then they'd all start yelling, and God was not a patient man.
``We need a new way to judge mankind, God, and by judging I mean kill and torture and beat to death,'' said Mut.
God rolled his eyes.
Mut was one of those gods that always had to act tough.
As if being a goddess with the power to change fate and the weather wasn't enough.
God crossed his arms over his chest and glared at her.
He'd let the humans stay alive far longer than she was worth.
God wasn't cruel, but he wasn't nice, either.
He had given the world a good chance at survival, and it had been slaughtered.
God didn't care about them one way or the other.
Humans were simply another test.

sentences.sentence: TV, same bland magazine covers, same magazines.
My dentist, Dr. Halden, seemed like he knew me pretty well.
Not a normal friendly dentist kind of well, but the kind of well a doctor might know a patient.
He was tall, in his early 50s I guess, and had a deep, rough voice.
He was also kind of gruff.
But again, I wouldn't call him mean, just rough.
I think he was trying to be friendly, but it always came off as kind of gruff.
Dr. Halden was a very good dentist, though.
I had worked with him for more than 10 years and only had one minor scare.
That scare was a broken tooth, and he fixed it well enough so I could chew food without it hurting.
When I woke up, Dr. Halden was there.
He looked down at me with a sort of pity I couldn't put a finger on.
As soon as I was out of the chair, my thoughts began to race.
Why was I in his waiting room, and how did I get there?
The only thing I could think of was that someone had come to take me.
Like, I had a broken leg or something.
Of course, this wasn't right.
My legs were fine, as was the rest of me.
I looked down at myself in the mirror above one of the waiting room chairs.
No scratches, bruises, no cuts.
I looked exactly as I had when I left the office.
So that theory was out the window.
Now, what was the most likely thing to happen?
The obvious answer was that something had gone wrong in the office, like Dr. Halden had forgotten to put one of my teeth under the drilling machine or something, and now he was bringing me to the ER.

sentences.sentence: Stripes, better than the Ramones, even better than the Sex Pistols and the Clash.
I was only a few years old, and my brain was still mush, but I could sense it: I had to listen to that guy.
It was all about cool.
I have always admired him: it was such an innocent admiration.
I didn't know a thing about drugs, I didn't know a thing about rock 'n roll and the sex.
All I knew was that, when he called, I had to drop everything and listen.
My mother used to beat the piss out of me for such indiscretions, and he'd be there to pick me up.
He'd make me listen to his latest hits over and over again, and I'd be back into the house a hundred times more confident than before.
He was a real friend, like I needed a friend.
I couldn't understand how he could just die.
I was so young, and I was still thinking 'cancer'.
I never thought about what really happened.
I sigh, and pick up the book again.
I look at it.
It's a book of love poems.
I laugh bitterly.
The last time I even heard of a love poem was in year 5.
He was trying to pass as a poet and failed.
Still, he was always in awe of Shakespeare.
`` You'll never believe this:' I begin.
I pause, wondering if I am going to be able to read this.
I close my eyes.

They'd say that radiation wasn't as big of a problem as it was made out to be, but when I asked if they would mind if I could spend some time there, they happily let me use their equipment as much as I wanted. 
 `` There we go.'' Said the man happily, smiling as he handed me the clipboard. 
 
 I looked it over, grumbling a bit. I really don't know what you're thinking when you decide to do this experiment on a teenager, but the results could come in handy. 
 
 As I finished taking notes, my cell phone rang, `` oh, crap, it's that bitch again.'' I quickly grabbed the phone, hoping to ignore her, but the message cut me off before I could. 
 
 The woman in my life had been a huge part of my life, and we were very much together, but now, we'd drifted apart. The distance was hard on both of us, and sometimes, it felt like we were forever apart, and that hurt the most.

sentences.sentence: patient, I can see her name in my head, it read Sarah.
I don't recall the day or date, only that I had just been to the hospital to observe a procedure and this was my first real patient.
Sarah sat there in the examination room smiling at me.
Her white teeth were clean and showed not a hint of plaque or tartar, her gums were pink and healthy looking, she did not have bad breath.
Her breath was sweet, her eyes were clear and they glistened with happy surprise when she saw me, she seemed like a healthy, happy woman.
I had just left my stethoscope hanging in the rack, after all, I thought, no one could see that I didn't know how to do anything.

I took my stethoscope out of my pocket, and placed it on my chest and took the earpieces from the ends, I placed them over my ears, and put the rest of the stethoscope around my neck, I went to my examination table and lay down, I placed my hands under my back and spread my legs, and I breathed in.
I could hear my own heartbeat in my ears, beating in a steady rhythm, it would stop for a while and then begin again, it sounded like the steady beat of a drum.
I heard a faint sound in my ears, and I realized it was Sarah's heart, I took off my ear pieces.
She was on a heart monitor, I could see her heart in real time, and her heart rate was low, it was a little over 60 beats per minute, it was a perfect rhythm, and the monitor showed it.
Her heart looked like it was playing its own beat, almost like she was the only one that could hear the music, and her heart seemed to play the only beat the world could hear.

Sarah sat there in the examination room smiling at me. Her white teeth were clean and showed not a hint of plaque or tartar, her gums were pink and healthy looking, she did not have bad breath. Her breath was sweet, her eyes were clear and they glistened with happy surprise when she saw me, she seemed like a healthy, happy woman. I had just left my stethoscope hanging in the rack, after all, I thought, no one could see that I didn't know how to do anything.
 
 I took my stethoscope out of my pocket, and placed it on my chest and took the earpieces from the ends, I placed them over my ears, and put the rest of the stethoscope around my neck, I went to my examination table and lay down, I placed my hands under my back and spread my legs, and I breathed in. I could hear my own heartbeat in my ears, beating in a steady rhythm, it would stop for a while and then begin again, it sounded like the steady beat of a drum. I heard a faint sound in my ears, and I realized it was Sarah's heart, I took off my ear pieces. She was on a heart monitor, I could see her heart in real time, and her heart rate was low, it was a little over 60 beats per minute, it was a perfect rhythm, and the monitor showed it. Her heart looked like it was playing its own beat, almost like she was the only one that could hear the music, and her heart seemed to play the only beat the world could hear.

It's the last time I take you out of this country if you don't answer.
The reason I brought you here was to prove it.
You are a cat, I know this.
I brought you here to prove it.
So you better say what you are or I'll show your masters what happens to you if you don't say anything.''
``But I thought I had proved it already by taking you out of your house and bringing you here.
I have cameras in your house, remember?
But, I wanted to confirm it in person.
And, what's the harm in telling me, it's just a cat, right?''
You were starting to think you had gone overboard and that it was all just a big misunderstanding and that he was just a normal cat.
But the more time passed, the more you began to believe it was true.
You didn't know why, but the cat was really talking to you.
In one piece of paper you found a map with a cat's paw printed on it.
The other piece of paper was a note with the following written on it.
`` I'm glad you decided to visit me.
You were probably wondering why I haven't visited you before.
I'm glad you wanted to help me escape my house.
I'm not saying you'll see everything about my house or your apartment though.
